title: Implement it from the page
description:
Two functions are documented below in the style of a reference page (lesson 1.02). Implement them so they behave **exactly** as described, edge cases included.


**`slice`**

```cpp-norun
std::string slice(const std::string& s, std::size_t pos, std::size_t count = std::string::npos);
```

Returns the part of `s` that starts at `pos` and is `count` characters long, or as many as there are if fewer than `count` remain.

- **Return value**: the characters in the range `[pos, pos + n)`, where `n` is the smaller of `count` and `s.size() - pos`. When `pos == s.size()` the result is empty.
- **Exceptions**: throws `std::out_of_range` if `pos > s.size()`.

**`lastChars`**

```cpp-norun
std::string lastChars(const std::string& s, std::size_t count);
```

Returns the last `count` characters of `s`. If `count` is at least `s.size()`, returns all of `s`. Never throws (except `std::bad_alloc`).
hints: Read the exception rule first: `pos == s.size()` is allowed and gives an empty string; only `pos > s.size()` throws.
`std::string::substr` already behaves almost like `slice`. Check its own reference page: which of these rules does it already follow?
